critical_code_review_comments: infra_projection.py (~335 lines) — clean separation: _safe_tz, _advance_to_sending_day, _local_date helpers + build_projection / aggregate_capacity / calendar_for_account public API. Correctly scopes drip + campaign queries to user_id for non-admin. Uses 2 Mongo round trips total (drips → contacts → campaigns), not N.

Drip projection round-robins across drip.account_ids correctly — verified at runtime that 5 contacts × 3 steps = 15 total projected sends, with first-send date showing 3+2 across the 2 inboxes (the round-robin remainder ends up on the alphabetically-first inbox).
Scheduled campaign spike distribution: pending=10, 3 accounts → 4/3/3 (one extra on the first account) — matches spec.
Horizon comparison uses `local_date >= horizon.astimezone(tz).date()` — correct boundary handling so day 119 is included but day 120 is not.

calendar_for_account: status mapping is independent per day, today uses live emails_sent_today counter so day-zero matches the rest of the dashboard exactly. Future days only see projected sends — correct.
_advance_to_sending_day has a 14-step paranoia cap — defensive against malformed schedule.sending_days. Sensible.

infrastructure_routes.py /inboxes endpoint now calls build_projection on EVERY request — for a workspace with ~100 accounts + ~50 drips + ~200 contacts this is one extra Mongo round trip per list call. Fine today; if a workspace scales past ~5k drip_contacts, consider memoising for the lifetime of a request or returning the per-account projection from a single shared call inside _load_inboxes. Non-blocking.

Wire-up: _summarise(rows, projection=…) signature stayed backward compatible — Phase-1 paths still work when projection is None (falls back to linear estimate with explicit note). Good defensive default.
Capacity card 'remaining_today' uses live counters (not projection) so today's number always matches the on-page Inbox Availability table — exactly what users expect.

Frontend Infrastructure.jsx: heat cell title attribute correctly composes `{date}: {used}/{limit} used ({remaining} remaining) — {status}` — accessible + screen-reader-friendly. Outside-click + close button both wired to close. Toggling calendar-table works (true unmount, not just hide).
